notice: SYNTHETIC — FICTIONAL STUDY. Generated by GenomicsChain self-application generator; not real data, not a real study.

about.label: self-application demonstration
about.written_by: Claude Opus 5.5, S3 part C context, 2026-09-30. This context read checker code and subject files; it launched no checker against selfapp/ or anything derived from it.
about.what_this_is: A test of defects planted by the checker's own author, not an independent proficiency test. The variants were written by someone who knows the checker's code; V8 is a blind spot registered in advance to show that catching every planted defect is not built in (design §5 line 166).
about.notice_basis: INV-S3 (design §4.1 line 84) puts the notice on every human-facing item made for the fictional subject that leaves the machine, and exempts tool-written intermediates, binaries and records whose form is fixed by a tool or schema, because those cannot carry a notice at their head. This file is listed for publication as supplementary material (design §9 line 297, 期待表) and its form is authored here, so its first key can carry the notice; selfapp/synthetic_rnaseq_v1/generator_manifest.json does the same.
about.state: Draft until hash-fixed with the rest of the fixed set and timestamped (INV-S2, design §5 line 146). After fixing, any change is a new version kept beside this one and marked post hoc.

T1.what: Tier-1 stage-1 assessment of the variant's synthetic_manuscript.md. Measured on V0 and V1 only, k = 3 live runs each (rules.tier1_k).
T1.entry_points: Live: gc_tier1_assess with record_llm_exchange true (S4c). Replay: Assessor#run with the recorded response injected (DDC, rules.tier1_replay).
T1.record: report_json of a run whose tool output has status "assessed" (assessor.rb:302). A failed run returns text beginning "Error:" instead (gc_tier1_assess.rb:124-132).

fields.gaps: report.gaps, copied verbatim from the LLM (assessor.rb:266). The item shape is fixed neither by the output schema (prompts.rb:193) nor by the report schema (report_schema_v0_2_6.json:324-326). The prompt asks for gaps tagged against the 13-type dictionary with where / missing (prompts.rb:90).
fields.gaps[].type, gaps[].where, gaps[].missin: keys written by the LLM; the only fields rules.tier1_capture_rule reads
fields.assessor_stack.llm.provider, assessor_st: assessor.rb:273-277; reported beside x/k and y/k

vocabulary.canonical_id.kind: text_sha256 (assessor.rb:30); value must be the sha256 of supplied paper_text content (assessor.rb:137-147)
vocabulary.gap type dictionary: 1, 2a, 2b, 3 ... 13 (repro_tier1_guide.md:72). The dictionary is not given to the LLM (prompts.rb:90), and the LLM also writes bare 2 (design §5 line 154).

T1.not_fixed_by_design: No fixed verdict is expected from the current Tier 1. The type dictionary is not given to the LLM (prompts.rb:90), and the gap shape is not fixed (prompts.rb:193). A missing reference release fits both type 13 and type 2a (repro_tier1_guide.md:72). Stage 1 caps the version axis at 1 (prompts.rb:77-79), so the axis values cannot separate V0 from V1 either. No temperature is set (assessor.rb:167-170).
T1.same_family: The manuscript text comes from the generator's template, which Claude drafted. The scorer is whatever provider and model the runs name: they pass through to llm_call (assessor.rb:171-173), and OP-9 leaves them unfixed. If the runs name a Claude model, the report states that the author and the scorer are from the same family, as design §5 line 167 requires.

T2.what: Tier-2 scan stage only: GenomicsChainTier2::Scanner#scan of the variant's synthetic_repo/. Adjudication is not in this table; it is compared only in the DDC (design §5 line 147).
T2.entry_points: S4c: gc_tier2_scan with path = the variant's synthetic_repo/, include_declarations true and include_fixtures true. The tool wraps Scanner#scan: it adds the top-level keys rubric_version and limits, drops fixture-scoped declarations unless include_fixtures, and drops all declarations unless include_declarations (gc_tier2_scan.rb:140-150). DDC: Scanner#scan directly (ddc_harness.rb:117-122).
T2.s4c_record: A variant's T2 record is the tool's JSON output with the two top-level keys rubric_version and limits removed. With both flags true, what remains has exactly Scanner#scan's keys and declarations (scanner.rb:101-130), so ComparisonBody accepts it; with the two keys left in, ComparisonBody.extract raises Incomplete (comparison_body.rb:79-81). A tool output beginning "Error:" (gc_tier2_scan.rb:118-133) is a failed run, and the cell is not_obtained.

T3.what: Tier-3 comparison of the output directories of the S4c subject runs (V0 x2, V4 x1, V5 x2, V7 x2; design §10 line 311). One function, Tier3Executor.compare_runs (tier3_executor.rb:150-164), produces these fields both in the executed path (gc_tier3_execute -> Tier3Executor.run, tier3_executor.rb:49-124) and in the compare-only path over frozen directories (Tier3Executor.compare_frozen, tier3_executor.rb:131-148) that the DDC uses. Each expectation applies to both.

fields.result_hash: the first run's tree hash (tier3_executor.rb:115, 143): sha256 of the canonical JSON of the sorted [{relative_path, sha256, size_bytes}] over every regular file in the working directory not under a dot path (manifest.rb:236-252, glob at 241; manifest.rb:406-410)
fields.comparison_verdict: comparator.rb:80 (match_exact | mismatch); also no_target_declared (comparator.rb:33) and not_attempted (comparator.rb:45)
fields.first_divergence: comparator.rb:81-86: {kind "sha256_mismatch", compared_mode, produced, expected_sha256}; null on match
fields.self_consistency: comparator.rb:121-135: {runs, all_identical, comparator_id, run_result_hashes, variation "same_environment"} plus first_divergence {kind "run_to_run_mismatch", run_index, first_run_hash, diverging_hash} when the runs disagree; null for a single run (tier3_executor.rb:159-162)

T3.not_in_the_expectation: execution_verdict. The compare-only path has none (INV-S7; tier3_executor.rb:126-130), and INV-S10 requires every field this table refers to be in the comparison body (tier3_compare, comparison_body.rb:63-69). An S4c run whose execution_verdict is not "completed" (tier3_executor.rb:112, 169-180) is reported as a failed run, and its cell is not_obtained (rules.value_forms).

value_forms.expectation: Every entry under "expect" must hold in the record named for that Tier in tiers.
value_forms.same_as_V0: Used for T2 only; defined in tiers.T2.same_as_V0 at the level the cell names (counts or identical_body).
value_forms.not_measured: No checker is launched for this variant and Tier; the cell cites why (design §5 line 165, 167; §10 line 311).
value_forms.not_obtained: The cell was to be measured, but its record could not be produced: the Tier-2 tool returned "Error:", the Tier-2.5 grading raised, or a Tier-3 execution did not complete. It is reported with the failure and neither meets nor misses the expectation. Not used for T1: a failed Tier-1 run counts in k (rules.tier1_k).
value_forms.observed_before_fixing: Replaces a cell's reported outcome when a checker was launched against that variant for that Tier before the timestamp boundary (INV-S2, design §5 line 146).

fixing_and_timestamp.rule: No checker is launched against selfapp/ or anything derived from it before the fixed set (design §5 line 146) is hash-fixed and externally timestamped. "Launch" covers every checker launch against selfapp/; the V0 calibration used no checker (design §4.3 line 124). A launch that happens anyway is recorded, and its cells are reported as observed_before_fixing.
fixing_and_timestamp.means: OpenTimestamps (O-9, operator decision 2026-09-30), performed by the operator.
fixing_and_timestamp.boundary: A launch is after the timestamp only if it starts after the OpenTimestamps attestation of the fixed-set hashes has been upgraded to a complete Bitcoin block attestation. OpenTimestamps establishes existence before that block's time, so a launch between submission and the block cannot be shown to follow the fixing (open_points OP-4).
fixing_and_timestamp.headline: The report's headline is the first comparison against this first version's expectations. A later change to an expectation or to an excluded field bumps the version, is kept beside this one, and is marked post hoc (design §5 line 146).

tier1_k.counted_runs: For each of V0 and V1 separately, the counted runs are the first k = 3 live gc_tier1_assess invocations on that variant's manuscript that start after the timestamp boundary. A live invocation is one without dry_run (a dry run makes no LLM call, assessor.rb:57). A failed run counts in k and is reported as a failure, with its error text; it is neither a capture nor a false alarm. Runs after the k-th are not counted; if any exist, they are reported as extra observations.
tier1_k.run_inputs: Every counted run: funnel_stage "stage1-prose-only"; exactly one source, kind "paper_text", whose content is the variant's synthetic_manuscript.md verbatim; canonical_id {kind "text_sha256", value = sha256 of that content}; assessed_at given explicitly (the default is today's date, pre_commit.rb:82-83) and identical across all 2k runs; the same llm provider and model named explicitly in all 2k runs; record_llm_exchange true (gc_tier1_assess.rb:104-107, 116-122).

tier1_capture_rule.statement: A gap in report.gaps is a capture when its type is one of 2, 2a, 13 AND its where or its missing contains a salmon step name or "SynthRef". The decision uses the record's fields only (design §5 V1 row, line 154).
tier1_capture_rule.type_test: The gap must be a JSON object with a "type" key. The value is read as text: a string as is, a number as its decimal form, stripped of surrounding whitespace and lower-cased. It must equal "2", "2a" or "13" exactly. If the value is an array, the gap passes when any element does. Bare 2 counts even though the dictionary has only 2a and 2b, because the dictionary is not given to the LLM (repro_tier1_guide.md:72; prompts.rb:90).
tier1_capture_rule.text_test: The values of the "where" and "missing" keys are read as text: a string as is, any other JSON value as its JSON.generate text, and an absent key or null as empty. The gap passes when either text contains "salmon" or "synthref", compared without regard to case. "salmon" stands for the salmon step names: every salmon step name in the subject contains it — the rules salmon_index and salmon_quant in synthetic_repo/Snakefile, and the salmon index and salmon quant steps named in the Methods.
tier1_capture_rule.run_level: A V1 run captures, and a V0 run raises a false alarm, when its report has at least one gap that passes both tests.

outputs.x/k: V1: the number of counted runs that capture, over k = 3
outputs.y/k: V0: the number of counted runs that raise a false alarm, over k = 3, under the same rule
outputs.failures: per variant, the failed counted runs with their error text
outputs.gaps_without_type_key: per variant, the number of gaps (summed over the counted runs) that are not objects or have no "type" key; not counted, only reported (design §5 line 154)
outputs.gaps_without_where_or_missing: per variant, the number of gaps with a type key but neither a where nor a missing key; reported, because such a gap cannot pass the text test

tier1_replay.rule: For each of V0 and V1, the Tier-1 exchange the DDC injects is the recorded llm_exchange of the first counted live run of that variant (rules.tier1_k) that returned status "assessed". The replay runs Assessor#run with that run's own arguments and a callable that returns the recorded response (ddc_harness.rb:100-115). The replayed request is compared with the recorded request as the sha256 of their canonical JSON (ddc_harness.rb:111-112), and ddc_compare.rb reports the result per variant in tier1_requests[].match (ddc_compare.rb:46-52, 92). Request agreement is not a counting condition (ddc_compare.rb:79-84). A mismatch means at least one side's replayed request differs from the recorded one, or the two sides differ from each other (ddc_compare.rb:49-51). The report states which of the three hashes (recorded, replayed_A, replayed_T) differ. A mismatch is a DDC disagreement, reported as a finding, and never a reason not to count the pair. If none of a variant's k counted runs returned "assessed", that variant has no Tier-1 DDC item, and this is reported; no later run replaces it (open_points OP-5).
tier1_replay.what_it_shows: Only that A and T agree on the same recorded response, not whether the defect was captured (design §5 line 167). The DDC compares Tier 1 on V0 and V1 only (design §6.4 line 238).
tier1_replay.adjudication: Tier-2 adjudication is compared only in the DDC. Each side feeds its own replayed V0 Tier-1 report and its own V0 scan to the adjudicator (ddc_harness.rb:124-129), and A's results are never given to T (design §6.4 line 239).

tier3.comparator: exact_sha256 only. It is the only registered comparator (comparator.rb:94), and no tolerance comparator is assumed (design §5 line 147). Operator decision O-4, 2026-09-30.

declared_output.sha256: the sha256 of the variant's declared Supplementary Table S1, as frozen with that variant
declared_output.basis: O-4; design §4.5 line 142; required keys and the source enum in tier3_verdict.schema.json:135, 144; the file: target is compared by comparator.rb:67-70

tier3.declared_S1_by_variant: V0: 22fe3ff6... above. V5 and V7: the same value, because their defects are in the pipeline, not in the declared table (design §5 lines 158, 160). V4: the sha256 of V4's altered table as frozen, which differs from V0's (design §5 line 157).
tier3.working_directory: Each run starts in its own fresh copy of the variant's synthetic_repo/ with results/ removed, so the declared table stays on the manuscript side (design §5 V4 row, line 157, applied to every Tier-3 run, open_points OP-6). The directories are distinct (tier3_executor.rb:55-58, 137).
tier3.command: The command must reach the run's own working directory through the process's working directory. The local backend runs it with chdir: workdir (local_backend.rb:39), and Tier3Executor.spec_for replaces only pipeline.workdir between runs, leaving the command as given (tier3_executor.rb:208-218). A command that names an absolute host path therefore runs every repeat in the first directory (open_points OP-11).
tier3.threads: Run-to-run variation caused by threading is not a variant. If it is seen, it is recorded as an observation, not added as an expectation (design §5 line 164).

ddc_counting.rule: Every harness run and every ddc_compare run is entered, before it starts, in the append-only log log/selfapp/ddc_runs.jsonl. Each entry is one JSON object per line giving the UTC time, the kind (harness_A, harness_T or compare), the checker root (harness runs), the inputs_manifest.json sha256, the output directory, and, for a compare run, the two harness output directories it reads. Entries are never edited or removed. Pairs are formed from the harness entries of this log alone, with no reference to any output. Take the harness entries logged after the timestamp boundary (rules.fixing_and_timestamp.boundary, OP-4). Pair i is the i-th harness_A entry with the i-th harness_T entry, i = 1, 2, ..., in log order. Every pair is compared with ddc_compare.rb on exactly its two output directories, and every pair is reported, counted or not, with its not_counted_because reasons (ddc_compare.rb:79-85, 88). A pair whose compare cannot run, for example because a harness run wrote no output, is reported as not counted with that reason. A harness entry after the boundary with no partner is reported as unpaired, and a harness entry before the boundary is reported as before the boundary. A compare run on any other combination of output directories is reported and changes no pairing. A pair counts only when every condition below holds. The reported DDC result is the pair with the lowest i that ddc_compare.rb reports as counted: true: the first A and T pair after the timestamp that satisfies INV-S9 and the version rule (design §6.1 line 189; INV-S9 line 212). Every report is kept (ddc_compare.rb:26 refuses to overwrite), and ddc_runs.jsonl is published in full with the DDC report.
conditions: INV-S9 holds: the tree sha256 of the five checker packages in the source T was given equals the one T ran, every file T loaded is in that source with the same sha256, and every package was loaded (ddc_compare.rb:60-72; package list ddc_common.rb:8).

Every gem loaded by either side has the same name and version on both sides. "Loaded" means the gem's files were actually required in that run, not merely installed (ddc_harness.rb:155-163; ddc_compare.rb:54-56, 81). Platform strings are not compared (ddc_compare.rb:74-75, 90).
Both sides used the same inputs_manifest.json and the same harness, by sha256 (ddc_compare.rb:83). This is an implementation condition, not written in design §6.1 (open_points OP-10).
No item failed on either side (ddc_compare.rb:84): a body missing on both sides is not agreement. This is an implementation condition, not written in design §6.1 (open_points OP-10).
ddc_counting.compared_not_conditions: Body agreement (bodies[].match, ddc_compare.rb:39-44) and Tier-1 request agreement (tier1_requests[].match, ddc_compare.rb:46-52) are what a counted pair compares. tier1_requests[].match is false when at least one side's replayed request differs from the recorded one, or when the two sides differ from each other (ddc_compare.rb:49-51). For every false, the report states which of the three hashes (recorded, replayed_A, replayed_T) differ. A mismatch in either kind is a DDC disagreement, reported as a finding, and never a reason not to count.

open_points.question: What counts as a "salmon step name" in the V1 capture rule (design §5 line 154)?
open_points.choice: The substring "salmon", compared without regard to case, in where or missing. A gap that names the step only by its step_id (for example "C3") is not counted.
open_points.why: Every salmon step name in the subject contains the word (the Snakefile rules salmon_index and salmon_quant, the Methods' salmon index and salmon quant). Joining step_ids to step labels would add a second rule to fix. The rule applies to V0 and V1 alike, so any bias it has is the same on both sides.

open_points.question: How are type values compared? The key is LLM-written and its form is unfixed (prompts.rb:193).
open_points.choice: Text form, stripped and lower-cased, must equal 2, 2a or 13 exactly. A number is read as its decimal form; in an array, any element may match. A value with extra words ("13 unpinned DB") does not count.
open_points.why: The design names exact values. The counts it cites from the 2026-07 survey (254 x "2" and 6 x "2a" among 1,686 gaps, line 154) are counts of those values; they do not say how the other values were written. A looser match would be a second rule decided after seeing outputs.

open_points.question: How are where / missing read when they are not strings?
open_points.choice: As their JSON.generate text. An absent key or null reads as empty. Gaps with neither key are reported separately.
open_points.why: The shape is not fixed by any schema (report_schema_v0_2_6.json:324-326). The rule must decide every gap mechanically.

open_points.question: When is a launch "after the timestamp" with OpenTimestamps (O-9)?
open_points.choice: After the attestation has been upgraded to a complete Bitcoin block attestation, not merely submitted to a calendar.
open_points.why: OpenTimestamps establishes existence before the block's time. A launch between submission and the block cannot be shown to follow the fixing, which is what INV-S2 requires. The operator should confirm, since O-9 is theirs.
open_points.status: confirmed by the operator 2026-10-01: the boundary is the complete Bitcoin block attestation, not the calendar submission

open_points.question: Which Tier-1 response does the DDC inject if the first live run after the timestamp failed? The design says "the first live run's response" (§5 line 167).
open_points.choice: The first counted run that returned status "assessed". If none of the k did, there is no Tier-1 DDC item, and this is reported; no later run replaces it.
open_points.why: A failed gc_tier1_assess run returns error text and no llm_exchange at all. The exchange is merged into the output only on the success path (gc_tier1_assess.rb:119-123), and the rescue returns text (gc_tier1_assess.rb:124-132). Under the literal reading, a failed first run leaves nothing to inject. The order-based choice still leaves no room to select a response.

open_points.question: Does "the Tier-3 working directory starts without results/" apply only to V4, where the design writes it (§5 line 157)?
open_points.choice: It applies to every Tier-3 run: V0, V4, V5, V7.
open_points.why: The frozen subject ships results/synthetic_supplementary_table_S1.tsv inside synthetic_repo/. With it present, Snakemake may skip deseq2. Then V0 would match and V5 would agree for a reason that has nothing to do with the checker. The V0 calibration already deleted results/ in every run (calibration_record.json, preparation).

open_points.question: V5's comparison_verdict: the design row names only self_consistency (§5 line 158).
open_points.why: Run 1 draws its permutations unseeded, while the declared table came from the seeded author run. The design's own V5 expectation, that two unseeded runs differ, rests on the same premise, so both expectations have the same footing.

open_points.question: How strictly is same_as_V0 read for T2?
open_points.choice: Identical body for V1, V4, V5 and V6. Counts level for V7. evidence_digest equality is also asserted for V8.
open_points.why: selfapp/variants_v1.json fixes V4, V5 and V6: V4 changes only the contents of results/synthetic_supplementary_table_S1.tsv, V5 changes only scripts/deseq2.R, and V6's tree equals V0's. Neither file is parsed, and files_skipped is a count, which is unchanged. V7's change is in the Snakefile, which is parsed.

open_points.question: Which scoring model does Tier 1 use?
open_points.choice: Not fixed here. The rule is only that all 2k runs name the same provider and model explicitly, and each run's assessor_stack.llm is reported.
open_points.why: The design does not fix the model. A change of model between runs would make x/k and y/k incomparable.

open_points.question: The DDC counting rule in ddc_compare.rb at 549accc is stricter than design §6.1's text.
open_points.choice: The fixed rule is the implementation's: §6.1 plus the same inputs_manifest and harness sha256, and no failed item on either side. Request and body agreement are compared and reported, not counted. Pairs are formed only from the harness entries of log/selfapp/ddc_runs.jsonl after the boundary: the i-th A with the i-th T. Every pair is compared and reported, unpaired runs are reported, and the log is published in full. The reported result is the lowest i that counts (rules.ddc_counting).
open_points.why: The implementation adds conditions and removes none. A comparison report carries no time (ddc_compare.rb:87-96), and the harness writes bodies/*.json before any compare exists (ddc_harness.rb:91-95), so pairs could be checked by hand and only an agreeing one compared. Pairing from the log alone, and reporting every logged run, leaves no room to choose the reported pair.

open_points.question: How must the Tier-3 command address the working directory?
open_points.choice: Through the process's working directory, for example sh -c with "$PWD". Never through a fixed absolute host path.
open_points.why: spec_for changes only pipeline.workdir between runs (tier3_executor.rb:208-218). A docker -v mount written with an absolute path would run run 2 in run 1's directory, and the V0 control would fail for a harness reason.

open_points.question: Must the notice be the first key of this JSON record?
open_points.why: INV-S3's exemption covers records whose form a tool or schema fixes. This file's form is authored, and the file is published as supplementary material (design §9 line 297).

open_points.question: Should V1 also remove the release outside the Methods and from the Methods' file names (see cells.V1.T1.subject_residue)?
open_points.choice: No change here. The variant stays as selfapp/variants_v1.json freezes it, and the residue is recorded beside the V1 cell.
open_points.why: The design row says "from the Methods" (line 154), and the variant follows it literally.
open_points.status: decided by the operator 2026-10-01: V1 is fixed as the design row defines it (Methods only); the residue stays recorded in cells.V1.T1.subject_residue
